note: Tau kwa is a style of firm, pressed tofu. FairPrice sells 'Fortune Tau Kwa' with no mention of tofu, so without this the item scored 0 coverage against the right product.
Bean curd is tofu; SG stores use both names. Listed BEFORE any bare-word rule so the phrase wins.

'Veg' is only 3 chars so the >=4-char partial-prefix rule gives it no credit against 'Vegetables' — 'Frozen Veg' scored 0.41 against 'Churo Frozen Mixed Vegetables'. Also fixes the search query, which returned no mixed-veg products at all.
Seen on FairPrice ('Del Monte Vege Plus').
Same meaning as mixed; stores use both. NB 'mix' and 'mixed' ALREADY unify — the stemmer strips -ed — so this group is about the other words.
Phrase only — bare 'variety' is too common to remap safely ('variety of flavours').
Abbreviation. Matters because chocolate is a flavoured-milk variant word.
Abbreviation. 'Organic' is a must-match keyword, so the short form must fold onto it.
FairPrice writes both 'Soy Sauce' and 'Soya Sauce'; the inventory item is 'Soy Sauce (light)'.
Malay for squid; the inventory item is 'Squid Ring (unbreaded)'.
Coating form. Folded so an '(unbreaded)' item excludes battered products too.
Tempura is a batter coating — 'CB Tempura Natural Calamari Rings' slipped past an (unbreaded) item without this.
Phrase used for coated products; bare 'fried' is left alone (stir-fried is not a coating).
Same animal, both used in SG. Folded so a prawn item matches either.

Wongbok is napa/Chinese cabbage — NOT the same as a round cabbage.
UK vs US name for the same herb.
Kang kong = water spinach / morning glory.

Apostrophe spelling — FairPrice's own title is "Osk New Family Japan Roast Tea - Pu'Er". Needed as its own entry because synonyms run on the RAW string, before punctuation is stripped, so no other pu-erh rule sees it.
Spaced two-word spelling (FairPrice: 'RedMan Mooncake Paste Pu Er Tea'). Does not touch the item's own 'Pu Erh' — \bpu er\b cannot match when an 'h' follows.
Indian name for sesame (gingelly oil = sesame oil).
Gula melaka is palm sugar; stores label it either way.
FairPrice uses BOTH spellings in one result set ('Greek Style Yoghurt' vs 'Greek Yogurt'). Without this they tokenise differently and the Greek yogurt item misses two of three real products.
Double-h spelling once used by the inventory item; no store spells it this way.
Sichuan pepper is spelled several ways.
Pinyin spelling of the same pepper.
Malay spelling of the fermented shrimp paste; the inventory item is 'blachan'.
Red lentil (masoor dhall) — spelling used in the inventory name.

Measured 2026-07-31: Sheng Siong returns 0 for 'lentil' and 10 real products for 'dhall' (Masoor Dhall Split, Toor Dhall, Channa Dhall). Folding this way puts 'dhall' into the search query, which is what the shop actually indexes; the bare 'Lentil' term is still searched too, so the FairPrice match is unaffected. Direction matters — mapping dhall->lentil would keep querying a word neither shop uses.
Plural. Needed explicitly because synonyms are applied BEFORE stemming, so \blentil\b never matches 'Lentils' — and 'Red Lentils' is how FairPrice titles it.
Lentil pulse/dish — dal / dahl / dhal all mean the same.
The most common store spelling ('Chana Dal', 'Toor Dal') — was the one variant missing.

MUST be listed before the bare 'omega 3' rule, or that one fires first and this phrase never matches. Drops 'enriched', which no SG shop prints on an omega-3 egg — FairPrice uses the word on BREAD ('Gardenia Enriched White Bread') and on exactly one unrelated egg ('Nuyolk Vitamins Enriched Eggs'). Requiring it excluded the very products the item wants (Chew's / Pasar 'Fresh Eggs - Omega 3').
Hyphenated form of the phrase above.

Collapses to ONE token on purpose. tokens() drops any token starting with a digit, so 'omega 3' and 'omega 6' both reduced to just ['omega'] and the matcher could not tell Chew's Omega 3 eggs from Chew's Omega 6. 'omega3' survives tokenisation and stemming intact.
Same collapse for omega-6, so it stays DISTINCT from omega3 rather than folding onto a bare 'omega'.

Muscovado is by definition an unrefined BROWN sugar, but every shop titles it 'Dark Muscovado Sugar' — never 'brown'. The item 'Muscovado Sugar (Brown)' therefore failed its own (Brown) requirement on all three FairPrice products. Adding the word rather than removing the requirement keeps the item's intent intact.
Danish — staged for a future Danish store; harmless on SG titles.
